subject: SDK Quickstart & Env Setup — Next steps and integration notes
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kahn <samir@techfin.ai>, Elena Rossi <elena@finlytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: SDK quickstart + env setup (next steps)

Thanks again for the call this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have alignment.

Summary from today's call:
- Goal: embed Redwood inference into TechFin's claims-processing pipeline (low-latency reranking + tool-calling for structured outputs).
- Recommended integration path: start with our SDK quickstart (Python or TypeScript) running locally, then move to a staging Dedicated instance for perf testing.
- Key technical asks from your team: auth options (API key vs service principal), routing between models for low-latency vs high-quality, and embedding + reranker guidance for near-duplicate detection.

Immediate next steps (suggested):
1) I will share the quickstart sample repo and a short integration checklist (attached).
2) Dev workshop: 60-90m session next week to walk through local setup, auth, and an embeddings demo — propose Tue/Wed 10am PT.
3) Dev deliverables: sample Docker Compose + env example, and a starter reranker config we can iterate on.

Notes on environment setup:
- Python/TS SDKs both supported. For local testing we recommend:
  * Python: create a virtualenv, pip install redwood-sdk, set REDWOOD_API_KEY (or use a service principal token if you prefer).
  * TypeScript: node 18+, npm install @redwood/inference, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in .env and use the provided example client.ts.
- Auth: API keys are fine for PoC. For CI and long-term staging we recommend service principals + short-lived tokens (we can share a sample auth flow).
- Routing: use the SDK client route parameter to send latency-sensitive traffic to the smaller quantized model and fallback to the high-quality model on cache miss. We'll share sample code.

I'll attach the quickstart bundle and checklist now. If you can confirm preferred time for the workshop and which stack you want to start with (Python or TypeScript), we'll send calendar invite and a pre-work repo link.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Great — glad the timing works. Answers inline below and attaching the quickstart bundle (zipped samples) + integration checklist.

Embeddings & reranker:
- We'll share a sample reranker.yaml in the repo. Typical starter config: candidate pool = top 100 embeddings, scoring model = redwood-re-rank-small, threshold = 0.75 for automated suggestions, tune down to 0.6 for recall-focused tasks.
- Typical doc size: 1-3KB per document (post-processed). For claims processing you can shard long docs into 512-token chunks and store chunk-level embeddings.

Docker/local testing:
- Included in the zip: docker-compose.yaml that starts the sample app, a small mock server (auth + mocked responses), and a script to switch between sandbox and hosted sandbox via env var REDWOOD_ENV=sandbox or REDWOOD_ENV=hosted.

Structured output/tool-calling:
- SDK supports function/tool calling with schema-first definitions. We recommend:
  1) Define an explicit JSON schema for the output (status:string, code:int, suggested_actions:array).
  2) Use the SDK's structured-mode (client.predict({schema: ...})) to enforce shapes on responses. The client returns a parsed JSON object and also the raw string — always validate server-side before acting on webhook triggers.
  3) For webhooks, use signed callbacks (we can provide verification headers) and implement idempotency on your side.

Workshop invite: I'll send a calendar invite for Tue, Feb 23 10:00am PT and include the repo link and pre-work (clone the repo, set REDWOOD_API_KEY to the sandbox token).

Attaching: redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip, integration-checklist.xlsx

Best,
Marissa
